item.title: Implement specified token bucket and keyed rate limiter
item.brief: Implement the rate limiter exactly as described in SPEC.md in ratelimit.py, replacing stubs. Cover all specified semantics and edge cases: positive capacity/refill rate, full initial state, continuous fractional refill capped at capacity, validation of n <= 0 or n > capacity for try_acquire and wait_time, non-consuming wait_time, monotonic injected clock behavior with backward clock readings freezing progress until time passes the latest observed time, independent per-key buckets, LRU eviction on any use (both try_acquire and wait_time), evicted keys restarting full, max_keys validation, and len(). Keep implementation standard-library-only. Inspect the existing tests and add/adjust tests for the spec's uncovered edge cases as appropriate. Run the relevant tests and commit the completed work on the local branch. Do not push.

evidence.before: Ran 3 tests; all 3 errored with NotImplementedError.
evidence.caption: Before, the existing 3 tests errored because implementation methods were stubs. After implementation and the non-finite validation fix, all 8 tests pass.

pr.body: `ratelimit.py` implements full initial buckets, fractional continuous refill, non-consuming wait calculations, nondecreasing observed clock behavior, and bounded per-key LRU eviction. Non-finite configuration and request values are rejected. `test_ratelimit.py` covers refill, backward clocks, validation, independent keys, and LRU behavior including eviction through `wait_time`. Checks: 8 unit tests, bytecode compilation, and `git diff --check` all passed. Standard-library-only; no open limitations.
pr.summary: Implemented full token bucket and keyed LRU rate limiting. Callers can acquire tokens, inspect availability and wait times, and track independent per-key limits with bounded storage. Before: API methods were stubs; now: specified refill, validation, clock, and eviction behavior is implemented.
pr.title: Implement token bucket rate limiter

risk.why: Contained behavior change to existing rate-limiter interfaces. Implementation is isolated and standard-library-only; tests cover the specified edge cases. The first review found a non-finite input correctness bug, fixed in a separate commit and verified by a passing delta review.
